question: Therapeutic hypothermia (cooling to 33–34°C for 72 hours) is effective and indicated for a term neonate with moderate-to-severe HIE if started within 6 hours of birth.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. Therapeutic hypothermia (whole-body or selective head cooling to 33–34°C for 72 hours) is the ONLY proven intervention to reduce death and disability in term neonates with moderate-to-severe HIE, provided it is started within 6 hours of birth. This 6-hour threshold is non-negotiable — missing it means the intervention cannot be offered.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The 6-hour window for therapeutic hypothermia is the most critical time-threshold in neonatal neurology. Cooling to 33–34°C for 72 hours reduces death and neurodisability in term neonates with moderate-to-severe HIE when initiated within 6 hours. After 6 hours, the secondary energy failure phase is already established and cooling is no longer beneficial.
